textbookText: H2O + Cl2 → HCl+ HClO HClO→ HCl + [O] SO2 + [O] + 2H2O→ H2SO4 SO2 + 2H2O + Cl2 → 2HCl + H2SO4 Br2 and I2 also react in similar manner. iii. Action with ferrous salt: Ferrous salts are oxidized to ferric salt by all halogens.
H2O + Cl2 → HCl+ HClO HClO→ HCl + [O]

4FeSO4 + 2H2SO4 + [O]→ 2Fe2(SO4)3 + H2O 4FeSO4 + 2H2SO4 + Cl2 → 2Fe2(SO4)3 + 2HCl + H2O Br2 and I2 also react in similar manner. iv. Action with thiosulphate (Na2S2O3): Cl2 and Br2 oxidize sodium thiosulphate to free sulphur.
H2O + Cl2 → HCl+ HClO HClO→ HCl + [O] Na2S2O3 + [O]→ Na2SO4 + S Na2S2O3 + H2O + Cl2 → Na2SO4+ 2HCl + S But I2 oxidizes Na2S2O3 to sodium tetrathionate (Na2S4O6). Na2S2O3 + I2 → Na2S4O6+ 2NaI

Activity: 23 Observe the picture carefully and answer the following questions: a. What do you mean by bleach? b. Can you list some examples of bleaching substances? c. What could be the reason for using chlorine as a bleach?

Halogens being good oxidizing agents show excellent bleaching action by oxidation. Fluorine being most reactive is not used as a bleaching agent as it destroys the substance to be bleached. Iodine is the weakest bleaching agent and is also not preferred for bleaching the substance. Bromine is a mild bleaching agent and is also not generally used to bleach a substance. Chlorine is a strong and excellent bleaching agent among all halogens. It bleaches different substances. Its bleaching action is irreversible and permanent due the production of nascent oxygen.
H2O + Cl2 → 2HCl + HClO (moisture) HClO → HCl + [O] Colored Material + [O] → Colorless material Cl2 is used to bleach hard substances like textiles, wood, paper and pulp etc.
